new_scholarship.description: KU Leuven's centrally funded master's scholarship, financed by donations to the KU Leuven International Scholarship Fund. For the 2026-2027 academic year one scholarship was available, awarded to an outstanding applicant to any eligible KU Leuven master's or advanced master's programme. Holders receive a full tuition fee waiver, pay only an annual administration fee of circa EUR 140, and receive an allowance of EUR 13,200 per academic year for a maximum of two academic years. One application covers this scholarship together with the Master Mind, ASEAN, Africa and Central and South America scholarships.
new_scholarship.deadline: Application deadline 15 January 2026, 23.59 CET (2026-2027 entry); applications opened 15 October 2025.
new_scholarship.application_period: Applications open in early October and close 15 January, 23.59 CET, for entry the following academic year (2026-2027 cycle: opened 15 October 2025, closed 15 January 2026).
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Open to all nationalities; applicants must be applying to an eligible KU Leuven master's or advanced master's programme, must have a high academic performance and potential, and their previous degree(s) should have been obtained outside Flanders. Applicants whose first language is not English must prove a good command of English (Online TOEFL 94, IELTS 7, or Cambridge CPE C2).
eligibility: All nationalities are eligible.
Study level: master's programmes (a restricted list of eligible programmes is published for each academic year).
The student has a high level of academic performance and potential; excellent study results reflected in a high Grade Point Average on the transcript of records.

Previous degree(s) should have been obtained at a higher education institution outside Flanders; international students who completed a credit mobility programme at a host Flemish higher education institution remain eligible.

Students already enrolled at a Flemish higher education institution are not eligible (only exception: international students enrolled in a specific preparatory programme who apply in the spring before starting the master's in September).
Students may not combine the Inspiring the Outstanding Scholarship with any other scholarship.

Applicants whose first language is not English must meet the English requirement; English-taught degree holders from Australia, English-speaking Canada, Ireland, New Zealand, the UK or the USA are exempt.

new_scholarship.description: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master Degrees are integrated international master's programmes jointly delivered by at least three higher education institutions from at least three different countries, at least two of which are EU Member States or Programme-associated third countries. The European Commission funds the programmes and offers EU scholarships to the best-ranked students worldwide at EUR 1,400 per month for a maximum of 24 months. Students apply directly to the institution running their chosen programme, usually between October and January for entry the following academic year.

Applicants may apply with a demonstrably equivalent level of learning if it is officially recognised in the degree-awarding country. Students from all over the world are eligible, and each master's website lists its own entry requirements.

new_scholarship.description: Central European University awards need-based financial aid on academic merit to admitted students who indicate their interest in the funding section of the CEU Application Form, and who must begin their studies at the Vienna campus in the fall of the academic year for which the award is made. At bachelor's level the aid is a Partial Tuition Award of up to 50% of the tuition fee, capped at EUR 4,000 per academic year. At master's level candidates receive a Master's Tuition Award covering 50% to 80% of the tuition fee, with a Full Tuition Award only in exceptional cases, plus an optional Master's Stipend Award of EUR 300 to EUR 750 per month. At doctoral level the CEU Doctoral Scholarship covers the full cost of tuition together with a monthly stipend. Candidates from any country may apply. Financial aid can be requested in admission Rounds 1 and 2 only.

programme_detail_official.description: The International Visegrad Fund awards Visegrad Scholarships for study or research to master's and post-master's students and researchers from twelve countries: Albania, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, Kosovo, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia and Ukraine. Applicants must have completed at least four semesters of university studies. The awards are for one or two semesters at institutions in Central and Eastern Europe, and within the In-Coming scheme master's scholarships can be awarded for one to four semesters. The Fund's stated purpose is to foster creativity and promote understanding between people across borders, looking for individuals pursuing innovative ideas in science and education who wish to engage in conversation on development and cooperation in the Visegrad region. Applications for the next round open on 1 January 2027.
